posts.name: Trajector
posts.cooked:
I think Fanatic’s power most involve some conscious expenditure of effort, rather than just whatever she believes becoming true. Think about if she ever played a shell game…

Tachyon, practicing: “Guess which cup the ball is under!”

Fanatic: “I followed it the entire time. I know it’s under this one.”

“Are you sure?”

“I know it.”

“Well, I think you’re in for a bit of a - HEY!”

This phenomenon could mean that any time Helena is tricked into believing something, or mistakenly believes something, it manifests as true. My theory is that she has to really fully internalize a belief for her powers to kick in. This is a reason why her vehicle for invoking her power is all couched in prayer and meditation.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
She doesn't do what she doesn't believe she can do.

That doesn't mean she can't.  Imagine one of us has the ability to fly if we reach terminal velocity.  The likelihood of us ever finding out we have that power is ridiculously low, because not many are going to go do things to reach that speed, nor are we going to try to fly once we get there.  We don't even try, because we don't believe we can.

Fanatic believes she is an angel (or something like it), and her use of her powers fits that belief.  She doesn't do things that she doesn't believe she can, probably because she doesn't think to try.  Maybe she can teleport, or change bodies, or cheat at cards, but those things aren't things she tries to do, because they don't fit what she believes she can do.

Essentially, as I understand it, inside her head she has a Fanatic box that contains her purpose and powers.  Her faith has been tested, resulting in using the powers she knows she has differently, her purpose and methods seem to have alterred slightly, but the powers she hasn't gone outside the box, she isn't testing what she can do, she's acting as if she has a certain set of powers, she might push those powers farther and find she can do those things more powerfully,, but she isn't trying to go outside the box and do things she doesn't believe she can.

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
Trajector:

I thought I heard C&A say that Fanatic's powers affect "herself" and "physical objects in contact with her." Also definitely key to her abilities is that she has to actually believe in the transformed state of things - so I 100% agree that she doesn't transform into one of Apostate's minions, because she doesn't really believe she is one.

We also know that she doesn't require extended contract with things she transforms, and they don't have to be things that belong to her. What she does in Consecrated Ground is get herself to believe that the graveyard is holy and Apostate won't be able to draw on the corpses any more, and so it becomes that way. But she doesn't OWN the graveyard, and she wasn't there for a long time.

It's not that she just believed the graveyard was supposed to be holy, therefore it was holy. It's that she believed  she  was capable of consecrating something, and doing it. That wasn't her power changing the world around her as she believed it to be; it was that she generated power in herself, then directed that power outwardly in a conscious and deliberate act.

 

It's like any of her attacks – the Idolator doesn't have a cross scarred into his face because Fanatic just believed he was supposed to; he has a scar because she generated cross-shaped power in herself and projected it at him. Apostate doesn't have a big scar because she believed he's supposed to be that way; he has a big scar because she sworded the crap out of him.

So it's not an example of the world spontaneously changing to fit what she believes; it's an example of her deliberately exercising her power through herself to create change.
